gd_alfa_romeo_8c_2300.name: Alfa Romeo 8C 2300 Corto Touring Spider "Touring"
gd_alfa_romeo_8c_2300.description:
v1.13 by ACTK
Add news LODs (animations working)
Add data to data.acd

"It’s hard to even conceive how courageous the drivers who raced these early open cars were. Their bravery inspired the race cars and super cars of today. Enzo Ferrari himself raced an 8C 2300 at the Circuito delle Tre Provence, taking second place in 1931. Built between 1931 and 1934 the model was bodied by top coach builders (carrozzeria) Zagato and Touring.

Underneath the hood are two four-cylinder motors facing back-to-back and mated in the middle at the flywheel. The cams and supercharger are driven by gears in the middle of that marriage.
These cars were expensive in their day and are priceless now. Driving the 8C, the great Tazio Nuvolari saw victory at the Grand Prix of Italy and Monaco. Lord Howe won the 24 Hours of Le Mans, and a pair of Italians won the 1932 Mille Miglia in one.
gd_alfa_romeo_8c_2300.author: GeroDa74

frazer_nash_tt_1934.name: Frazer Nash TT Replica
frazer_nash_tt_1934.description: Founded by cyclecar designer Archie Frazer-Nash in 1922, the Frazer Nash company produced a series of unique and iconic pre-war sports cars. Known mainly for their chain-driven transmissions, the "chain gang" Frazer Nash cars were successful as road-going sports cars and in racing. The TT Replica model was based on the cars that contested the 1931 RAC Tourist Trophy Race. Although none of the cars entered that year actually finished the event, the TT Replica fared well in races from its introduction in 1932 until the end of production in 1939. Power was provided by three different engines - a modified 1,500 cc Meadows engine, or a 1500 cc engine produced in-house, designed by Albert Gough, or lastly the 1,660 cc 6-cylinder Blackburne engine, which required a slightly longer wheelbase to fit into the chassis. The example presented here is powered by the Meadows engine, which was fitted with a Gough-designed cylinder head, to produce a peak output of around 62 horsepower.
frazer_nash_tt_1934.author: T2Beatnik

bugatti_type_57g.name: Bugatti Type 57G
bugatti_type_57g.description:
The first French winner of Le Mans since 1926, the iconic Bugatti 57G took its place in racing history by winning the 1937 race. Car no.2, alternately driven by Jean-Pierre Wimille and Robert Benoist, quickly took and held the lead, it's streamlined shape reportedly giving it a clear advantage in fuel economy, allowing it to lap more and pit less.

Although a possible one-two was thwarted by the no.1 car (driven by Roger Labric and Pierre Veyron) retiring after 130 laps, Wimille and Benoist covered a record-breaking 3287.938 kms or 243 laps, 7 more laps (103km/64 m) than the second place Delahaye 135 CS, at an average speed of 136.997 km/h. A lead that might have been greater but for an 11 minute pause to recover the car after an accident. Roger Labric also set the race's fastest lap of 5:13 before his car's retirement.

A modified and supercharged variant of the car won again in 1939. A success that was quickly overshadowed by the tragic death of Jean Bugatti (Ettore Bugatti's eldest son), the driving force behind the car's development, on August 11th 1939 whilst testing the car at high speed.
bugatti_type_57g.author: Nicecuppatea
